hero.lead: A nation of 131.9 million where World Bank Group operations have helped mobilise nearly $12 billion of private capital, and a $500 million guarantee is drawing more into infrastructure.

capital.heading: Mexico draws private capital at scale. Next, safe water in every home.

Private capital World Bank Group operations helped attract in Mexico, fiscal years 2022 to 2026: nearly $12 billion
Disaster and climate resilience: Mexico’s first Catastrophe Deferred Drawdown Option, October 2026
Credit enhancement for sustainable and resilient transport, December 2025: about $1 billion of private capital expected

register.name: Disaster and climate resilience, Catastrophe Deferred Drawdown Option
register.detail: Approved 21 October 2026 · Cat DDO · Three years, with the possibility of extension
register.text: Contingent financing Mexico can draw on after a natural disaster, a climate shock or a public health emergency, with resilience work in areas such as infrastructure, housing, energy and health. Money that arrives fast after a disaster keeps homes, water systems and clinics running.

register.name: Building Sustainable Value Chains Project
register.detail: Approved 10 July 2026 · IBRD
register.note: Sustainable value chains for Mexican firms
register.text: An IBRD loan approved by the World Bank Board in July 2026 for more sustainable value chains among Mexican firms. Its project documents have not yet been read in these reviews.

register.name: Credit Enhancement Platform for Sustainable and Resilient Transport
register.detail: Approved 18 December 2025 · Credit enhancement of up to $500 million · Local Currency Mobilization Facility
register.note: About $1 billion of private capital expected for transport
register.text: Banobras, as trustee of the National Infrastructure Fund (FONADIN), uses the instrument to strengthen the guarantees the fund already gives, so that private lenders finance sustainable and resilient transport infrastructure, in local currency. Roads and transport connect citizens to jobs, schools and clinics.

register.name: Flexible Credit Line
register.detail: Approved 13 November 2025 · Two years · SDR 17.8254 billion · 200 percent of quota · Precautionary
register.note: Succeeds the 2023 line of about $35 billion
register.text: A two-year IMF arrangement that Mexico treats as precautionary: a line it can draw on if needed. The new line of about $24 billion is smaller than the SDR 26.7381 billion (about $35 billion) arrangement of November 2023 it succeeds.

register.name: Sustainable Communities for Climate Action in the Yucatán Peninsula (ACCIÓN, SAP049)
register.detail: Approved 20 February 2025 · Grant · Under implementation · Total value $32.7 million
register.note: About 2.3 million people with increased resilience
register.text: A Green Climate Fund grant through the Mexican Fund for the Conservation of Nature (FMCN) for climate action by communities of the Yucatán Peninsula. It protects the water, land and livelihoods of rural and coastal families.
by: Fondo Mexicano para la Conservación de la Naturaleza

register.name: Basin Approach for Livelihood Sustainability through Adaptation Strategies (BALSAS, FP236)
register.detail: Approved 18 July 2024 · Under implementation to 2031 · Total value $91 million
register.note: About 3.3 million people with increased resilience
register.text: Green Climate Fund financing, through IFAD, for climate adaptation by farming communities in river basins, with women, youth and indigenous peoples among its priorities. It protects the food and livelihoods of smallholders.

register.name: Sustainable and Inclusive Finance Development Policy Loan
register.detail: Approved 3 June 2024 · IBRD · Development policy loan
register.note: Budget support for sustainable and inclusive finance
register.text: IBRD budget support for reforms in sustainable and inclusive finance. Access to finance is how small firms and households invest in their livelihoods.

register.name: Catastrophe bond, Pacific hurricanes
register.detail: Issued 15 May 2024 · Four years
register.note: Takes Mexico’s 2024 cat bond cover to $595 million
register.text: A catastrophe bond issued by the World Bank (IBRD) that pays Mexico if a named storm on its Pacific side meets set criteria. Parametric cover pays quickly, so reconstruction of homes and services can begin at once.

register.name: Catastrophe bonds, earthquakes and Atlantic hurricanes
register.detail: Settled 17 April 2024 · Matures 24 April 2028 · Class A $225 million and Class B $70 million, earthquake · Class C $125 million, Atlantic named storms
register.text: Three classes of catastrophe bonds issued by the World Bank (IBRD) that insure the Government of Mexico against earthquakes and Atlantic named storms, replacing earlier bonds for these perils and adding $60 million of cover. Payouts are triggered when an event meets set location and severity criteria.

register.name: Credit line for conventional power generation
register.detail: Announced 22 June 2026 · Credit line of up to $500 million · Guaranteed by CFE
register.note: For the Federal Electricity Commission’s generation projects
register.text: A credit line from the Central American Bank for Economic Integration to the trust for conventional generation projects, guaranteed by the Federal Electricity Commission (CFE). It finances power generation for the national electricity system.
by: Central American Bank for Economic Integration

register.name: Environmental infrastructure in the State of Sonora
register.detail: Certified 13 February 2026 · Loan of up to MXN 650 million · 27 wells in 15 municipalities
register.text: A NADBank loan to Sonora to rehabilitate, relocate and equip 27 water wells, replace worn water lines in nine localities and improve wastewater collection and treatment. It reaches the water and sanitation standards directly.

register.name: Investment grant for nature-based farm loans, through FIRA
register.detail: Approved by the IDB Board · Investment grant from Germany’s International Climate Initiative · Nine states
register.note: About 3,000 small farmers; about $30 million of loans
register.text: An IDB grant that funds partial credit guarantees through FIRA, so lenders finance small farmers’ investments that protect soils, water and ecosystems, mainly in regions with high poverty. It reaches food and rural livelihoods.

register.name: Green buildings credit line with Nacional Financiera
register.detail: Signed late 2024 · Announced 26 March 2025 · AFD $75 million · Green Climate Fund $25 million (PEEB Cool)
register.text: A credit line from AFD and the Green Climate Fund to Nacional Financiera (NAFIN) for sustainable construction that saves energy, cuts emissions and uses water responsibly. Cooler, efficient buildings lower household and business energy bills.

register.name: 200-megawatt solar photovoltaic plant, EDP
register.detail: Announced 19 October 2026 · IFC loan
register.text: An IFC loan for a 200-megawatt solar photovoltaic power plant in Mexico developed by EDP. With a second EDP investment announced at the same time, IFC expects better electricity supply for about 200,000 people and more than 4,400 jobs.

register.name: Banca Mifel green bond
register.detail: Approved 21 July 2026 · Not yet signed · IDB Invest up to $75 million of an issue of up to $160 million
register.text: IDB Invest would buy up to $75 million, about 47 percent, of a thematic bond by Banca Mifel, whose proceeds expand the bank’s green sub-loans. It channels finance to clean energy and efficient buildings.

register.name: Fibra Nova industrial parks
register.detail: Announced 15 July 2026 · IDB Invest long-term loan up to $100 million · DEG up to $50 million
register.text: Long-term finance for the construction and operation of industrial parks, mainly in the state of Chihuahua. Industrial parks house the manufacturers that create formal jobs.

register.name: Lottus Education, equity
register.detail: Announced 4 June 2026 · Direct equity in a round led by Kans Capital
register.text: IDB Invest equity for Lottus Education to invest in infrastructure, equipment and its technology platform. Lottus teaches upper-secondary, undergraduate and graduate programmes, online and in person, to more than 90,000 students, more than 35,000 of them online.

register.name: Engen Capital, equipment finance along the border
register.detail: Signed 13 April 2026 · Loan of MXN 400 million (about $23.2 million)
register.text: A NADBank loan to Engen Capital to finance energy-efficient industrial equipment, cleaner freight and passenger transport and expanded wastewater treatment for communities along the border with the United States.

register.name: Banco Inmobiliario Mexicano sustainable bond
register.detail: Announced 20 March 2026 · Sustainable bond subscribed by IDB Invest · About $46 million
register.text: A sustainable bond by Banco Inmobiliario Mexicano (BIM) that expands its lending to small and medium builders of housing in vulnerable areas. It reaches shelter, in a nation where IDB Invest cites 15 million households living in inadequate conditions.

register.name: Carbonwave, sargassum processing
register.detail: Announced 3 March 2026 · Convertible loan · Four years
register.text: IFC finance for Carbonwave, which processes the sargassum seaweed that reaches the coast at its plant in Puerto Morelos, to scale up its operations and research. It protects coastal livelihoods in tourism and fishing.

register.name: IENTC broadband network
register.detail: Announced 5 February 2026 · Revolving credit line · $8 million committed · $12 million uncommitted
register.note: More than 3 million people, over half of them in poverty
register.text: IDB Invest finance for IENTC to extend its fibre-optic network in regions with low broadband, including the south and south-east. Connectivity opens education, health services and work online.

register.name: Scotiabank Mexico, housing finance for women
register.detail: Announced 18 December 2025 · IFC investment of up to $250 million
register.note: 4.5% of women have a mortgage, against 7.2% of men
register.text: IFC finance for Scotiabank Mexico to expand mortgages for women, in a nation with a housing shortage of 9 million units. It reaches shelter directly.

register.name: Grupo Naturasol, food processing
register.detail: Announced 24 September 2025 · Senior secured loan
register.text: An IFC loan for new production lines and infrastructure in Grupo Naturasol’s potato and corn processing, which sources mainly from Mexican farmers. It reaches food and farm livelihoods.

register.name: CFE Fibra E, inaugural bond
register.detail: Announced 11 September 2025 · IFC $75 million anchor investment in a $725 million issue · Over $6 billion of demand
register.text: IFC anchored the first bond of CFE Fibra E, which finances the strengthening and expansion of Mexico’s electricity transmission network. Transmission carries power to homes, schools and clinics.

register.name: CADU, green housing
register.detail: Announced 13 August 2025 · Five-year revolving credit line of up to MXN 700 million (about $35 million)
register.note: More than 17,000 social and middle-income homes, 2025 to 2030
register.text: IDB Invest working capital for green housing by CADU, a Mexican developer working mainly in Quintana Roo. It reaches shelter directly.

register.name: BEEL Sustainable Credit II fund
register.detail: Announced 7 May 2025 · IFC up to $30 million · Fund target up to MXN 8 billion (about $400 million)
register.text: An infrastructure credit fund managed by BEEL Infrastructure Partners in Mexico City that lends to digital, energy, transport, logistics, and water and sanitation projects.

register.name: Sustainable asset-backed securities of four non-bank lenders
register.detail: Announced 22 October 2024 · Issue of up to MXN 339 million (about $17.3 million) · Programme of up to MXN 1.5 billion
register.text: IDB Invest bought most of the first public joint issue in Mexico by four non-bank lenders (CRESCA, Proaktiva, Sefia and SFI), backed by their loans to micro, small and medium enterprises in agribusiness. NADBank and other investors took the rest. It reaches food and rural livelihoods.

register.name: Regenera Ventures I
register.detail: Announced 18 April 2024 · Investment of up to $4 million
register.note: A women-led fund for regenerative enterprises
register.text: A DFC investment in a fund backing Mexican companies in farming, forestry, eco-tourism and aquaculture that restore land, marine and coastal ecosystems, with USAID support in Chiapas, Oaxaca and the Yucatán Peninsula.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 80 in every hundred live in towns and cities; the rest live on the land they farm and fish.
items.alt: A busy street in Mexico City

items.name: The Land
items.label: Of land in farms and pasture
items.text: The land that feeds the nation, and the first place a citizen dividend can be earned.
items.alt: Agave fields in the highlands of Jalisco, Mexico

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of land under forest
items.text: Standing forest holds the water, soil and carbon that the world will pay to keep.
items.alt: Pine and oak forest in the mountains of Michoacan, Mexico

items.name: The Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water per person
items.text: Enough to supply every home, once it is stored, treated and piped.
items.alt: Turquoise water of a cenote in the Yucatan, Mexico

items.name: The Power
items.label: Of energy from renewables, 2021
items.text: Sun, wind, water and biomass already carry part of the load; the rest is the opportunity.
items.alt: A solar park in the Sonoran desert, Mexico

items.name: Grupo Naturasol
items.text: A Mexican processor of potatoes and corn that employs more than 3,700 people and sources mainly from Mexican farmers. IFC lent it US$30 million in September 2025 for new production lines.

items.name: CADU
items.text: A Mexican housing developer working mainly in Quintana Roo, with homes sold in six states. IDB Invest opened a credit line of up to MXN 700 million in August 2025 for green housing, towards more than 17,000 social and middle-income homes from 2025 to 2030.

items.name: EDP
items.text: An energy group with renewable power operations in Mexico, where IFC lent US$222 million in October 2026 for a 200-megawatt solar photovoltaic plant.

items.name: Lottus Education
items.text: A technology-driven higher education platform founded in 2015, teaching more than 90,000 students across Mexico, more than 35,000 of them online, in upper-secondary, undergraduate and graduate programmes. IDB Invest took an equity stake of 200 million pesos in June 2026.

items.name: Salud Digna
items.text: A clinical laboratory and diagnostic network of about 240 clinics across Mexico, serving nearly three million people a month and focused on the most common conditions, such as diabetes and hypertension. It reinvests what it earns in its own growth.

items.name: Banco Compartamos
items.text: A microfinance bank lending to micro and small enterprises, with a focus on women. IDB Invest and the IDB lent it up to the equivalent of US$50 million in pesos, signed in April 2022.
